title: Huhtamaki India Ltd - 509820 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Huhtamaki India Q3 net sales rose about 24% to INR748 crore with volume up about 7%, while reported PAT fell 19% to INR30 crore on a one-time Baddi charge.
summary.overview: Net sales reached about INR748 crore, up roughly 24% YoY and the highest quarterly sales in the last couple of years, with growth split across pricing pass-through, mix and volume. Reported EBIT was flat YoY because the prior-year quarter had one-time retirement-related gains; management says like-for-like EBIT margin is about 8% and EBITDA improved about 18% on a comparable basis. PAT fell 19% to about INR30 crore (from INR37 crore) after a INR96 million charge for closing the Baddi labels plant, with volumes moved to Ambernath and Bangalore. Nine-month sales grew about 16%, EBITDA about 25% to INR204 crore (margin about 10% vs 9.2%), and PAT about 13%.

segments.name: Flexible packaging
segments.commentary: Growth attributed to pricing pass-through of raw material inflation, mix shift to higher-value products and about 7% volume growth in Q3. Management says roughly one-third each from price, mix and volume, though exact split not given.

segments.name: Labels (pressure-sensitive)
segments.commentary: Baddi labels plant closed (about two months' notice, closing around the call date); volumes moved to Ambernath and Bangalore plants. Management says Baddi was the smallest plant by output and headcount and was not profitable.

guidance_outlook: No formal margin or full-year forecast given; management says it does not disclose forecasts.
Management aspires to grow every quarter and year and to keep improving margins, contingent on market conditions.
Sees no major capex needed for the next 2-3 years to meet demand, as productivity gains free up capacity.
Q3 EBITDA margin dip attributed to raw material cost spike in late September not passed through in the same month; expected to be recovered in following months.
capex_capacity: Baddi labels plant closed in Q3 with a INR96 million one-time charge; volumes shifted to Ambernath and Bangalore, which management says have spare capacity.
Solar captive generation at Khopoli started in August (Q3), lifting renewable electricity share to 23%.
Daman land is held for sale; bids being evaluated, no price disclosed, and sale to be disclosed to the market when concluded.
Management says no significant investment needed for next 2-3 years to meet demand; capacity utilisation figure not disclosed.
demand_pricing: Pricing is linked to raw material inflation through contractual pass-through, with lags of days to weeks; September RM spike was not fully passed through in the quarter.
Power and fuel cost inflation linked to Middle East prices is being pushed into pricing; other expenses rose to INR112 crore from INR96 crore YoY, partly due to prior-year one-time reversals.
Management claims volume growth while some customers report flat or declining volumes, implying market share gains; company holds less than double-digit share in a fragmented market.
Segment focus on higher-value products; weaker in commoditised single-layer segments such as biscuits, with pharma cited as a growth opportunity.
Regulatory PCR (recycled plastic content) mandates exist: about 30-40% for simple mono-material laminates, about 10% for complex multi-material laminates, rising annually.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin moderation is from inventory costs, are margins sustainable, and how is the INR150-170 crore top-line increase split between volume and price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said price, mix and volume contributed roughly equal shares, about one-third each. Like-for-like EBIT margin is about 8%; Q3 dip was timing of RM pass-through, expected to reverse next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: At what utilisation are plants running, and how much extra revenue could full utilisation add?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a utilisation figure or revenue capacity estimate; said there is enough capacity for the next 2-3 years without major investment, with productivity gains creating headroom.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any Baddi-style restructuring planned at other plants, and how will Baddi customers be served?
qa_highlights.answer: Baddi customers were moved to Ambernath and Bangalore and the supply chain is running smoothly. No similar restructuring planned at other plants currently; actions will be taken as demand requires.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise and will they stay elevated?
qa_highlights.answer: Partly base effects from one-time retirement reversals in the prior year, plus higher power and fuel costs linked to Middle East prices, CSR spend and provisions; management says these are factored into pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Can PBT margin rise to 10-13% through price increases and cost cuts, and how is AI being used?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said price increases are limited by commodity-linked frameworks; margin gains will come from mix and productivity. AI projects in operations, quality and safety have just started, with outputs to be shared later.

qa_highlights.question: What is the land held for sale, and what is its value?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give land area or price; the Daman plant land is being sold through a bidding process, and the sale will be disclosed when completed.

risks_watch: Sustainability of volume growth, given customers report flat or falling volumes and management has not quantified the mix of growth.
Pass-through lag on RM and energy cost inflation, which hit September and may affect the next quarter's EBITDA margin.
Q4 and beyond: whether like-for-like EBIT margin (~8%) holds and whether EBITDA margin stays near 10%.
Baddi closure savings and any further restructuring charges; PAT was hit by the INR96 million charge.
Daman land sale proceeds and timing, to be disclosed once concluded.
Regulatory PCR mandates could shift spec and product demand, and the timing of enforcement is uncertain.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume growth and the 9-month profit trend, but guarded on forward margins and tailwinds; management repeatedly declined to give guidance, pricing or land valuation figures, and said there are no structural changes to the business.
key_quotes: So if you look at comparable basis, we were almost 18% up year -on-year for the third quarter.
So at the moment, we see that we do not have any issue at least for next 2 year to 3 year cycle where we wouldn't need to do any huge investment to meet the market demand or increase in our volumes.
But in terms of tailwinds, I don't see many tailwinds.
